To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
media freedom has traditionally been justified by reference to its instrumental role in facilitating the democratic process.

1) the impact of online speech on political debate has been overestimated; 2) online speech has increased the power of a small number of individuals; and 3) media freedom should be understood as a form of individual freedom.
The Internet has increased the number of individuals able to participate in public political debate and the range of issues they may discuss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the Internet on the theory of media freedom, which is a topic of increasing relevance to legal scholarship.
the relationship between the media and political debate.
how the Internet has impacted on political debate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
media freedom in the digital era is a complex concept that requires a more nuanced approach than that of the mass media era.
the Internet has not changed the fundamental approach to media freedom.
the media freedom of the individual is of greater importance than it ever has been, but that this is not a sufficient reason for abandoning the instrumental justifications for media freedom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Internet is not a new medium, it is a new technology that is used for the same purposes as the old media.
media freedom is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for the flourishing of a democratic society.
the Internet is a new and powerful medium for political debate, but that the traditional justifications for media freedom remain valid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while media freedom has been a key component of the liberal democratic order, it is not a static concept that remains the same over time.
media freedom in the digital era requires a nuanced understanding of the role of the speaker and audience.
media freedom is not an all-or-nothing concept, but rather a matter of degree, with different rules applicable to different speakers and different media.
